input: What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?

output.answer: On its most recent earnings call (October 1, 2026, for fiscal Q1 2027 ended August 31, 2026), Nike shifted to a full-year guidance framework and did not give a standalone profit/revenue forecast for the current quarter (fiscal Q2 2027, ending November 30, 2026): CFO Dave Denton said Nike will 'provide a view of our expectations for the full fiscal year and update that perspective as the year progresses.' For fiscal 2027 Nike guided revenue to decline by a high-single-digit percentage, EBIT to fall by a greater percentage than revenue, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.15–$1.35 (excluding ~$0.15 of Pace restructuring charges), with a mid-20s percent tax rate. The only quarter-specific guidance was for Q2: management flagged an approximately 400-basis-point revenue headwind from lapping EMEA Cyber Week promotional activity and a higher North America sell-in comparison. The stock reacted negatively: NKE fell roughly 3–6.6% in extended trading on October 1 (Nasdaq after-hours quotes show a drop from a $35.10 close to $32.78, -6.6%, before recovering to $33.85, -3.6%, just before the call) because the EPS guidance sat far below the $1.61 consensus, and shares dropped again on Friday, October 2, for a second straight day of declines.
caveats: Nike did not issue quarter-specific revenue or EPS guidance for fiscal Q2 2027; the 400-basis-point headwind is the only quarter-level quantification, and the full-year outlook may be refined at Nike's Investor Day on November 16-17, 2026.

After-hours moves are thin and can reverse before the next session; different trackers quoted different after-hours declines (roughly 3% per CNBC, up to 6.6% per Nasdaq quotes cited by StockTitan, 6.24% to $32.96 per Investing.com).
The exact October 2 closing price was not verified from a fetched page; only that shares dropped again on Friday, October 2, for a second straight day.

passages.quote: Now I'd like to just spend a few minutes discussing our outlook for fiscal '27. And before I discuss the outlook, let me share my approach to guidance. I believe guidance should be grounded in the realities of the business, informed by both the risk and the opportunities ahead of us and set at a level that we believe is reasonable and attainable based on the information we have today and importantly, the actions we are taking to drive the business forward. One of my objectives is to build on our financial discipline and provide investors with a clear framework for understanding our performance as well as our outlook. To that end, beginning today, we intend to provide a view of our expectations for the full fiscal year and update that perspective as the year progresses.
passages.publisher: NIKE, Inc. (official Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript)

passages.quote: Starting with revenue. For fiscal '27, we currently expect revenues to decline in the high single-digit range. As Elliott outlined, we are making deliberate choices across portions of the portfolio, particularly in NIKE Sportswear, the Jordan Brand and Greater China to improve the health of these businesses over time. We will continue to take actions to reduce supply across key parts of the marketplace in support of a healthier marketplace environment and stronger full-price realization. We expect those actions will create pressure on reported revenues for the remainder of fiscal '27 and into '28. And as a reminder, in the second quarter, we are also lapping significant promotional activities in EMEA from Cyber Week and a higher comparison of North America sell-in activities versus last year. These 2 items will represent a headwind of approximately 400 basis points to revenues in the second quarter. While these decisions can dampen near-term top line results, our focus is on improving the quality of revenue and creating a more sustainable foundation for long-term growth.
passages.publisher: NIKE, Inc. (official Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript)

passages.quote:
**_Revenues_** are expected to decline high-single digits in fiscal 2027_._

**_Effective tax rate_** for fiscal 2027 is expected to be in the mid-20 percent range, subject to changes in earnings mix and discrete tax items.

**_Adjusted Diluted earnings per share\*\*_** is expected to be in the range of $1.15 to $1.35, which excludes approximately $0.15 of restructuring expenses related to Pace for fiscal 2027.

The company also offered a full-year outlook, saying it expects revenues to decline by a high-single digit percentage in fiscal 2027. Nike also said it expects adjusted earnings per share to be in a range of $1.15 to $1.35.

Shares of Nike fell roughly 3% in extended trading Thursday.

Nike shares closed at $35.10 on October 1, down 0.85% on the day and the lowest close since the November 2021 peak, before the release came out at 4:15 p.m. ET. [Nasdaq’s after-hours quotes](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/nke/after-hours) show the stock dropping to $32.78 at 4:20 p.m., 6.6% below the close, then recovering part of that to $33.85 at 4:57 p.m., 3.6% lower, just before the earnings call began. Nike’s results have moved the stock sharply before. The session after each of the last six reports brought moves between a 15.5% fall (April 2026) and a 15.2% gain (June 2025), based on Nasdaq’s closing prices.

Nike expects revenue to fall by a high-single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027, which runs to May 31, 2027, and [adjusted earnings](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/gaap-vs-non-gaap-earnings) of $1.15 to $1.35 a share. The adjusted figure leaves out about $0.15 a share of restructuring costs for the Pace program described below, so earnings under [GAAP](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/gaap-vs-non-gaap-earnings) accounting would come to roughly $1.00 to $1.20. The tax rate should be in the mid-20s, above the first quarter’s 22.7%. The release gave no forecast for the second quarter, and Hill said on the June call that Nike would share "the next phase of our growth strategy" at an Investor Day on November 16 and 17, per Nike’s [official transcript](https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/NIKE-Inc-Q4FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf).

*   Nike Q1 FY2027 EPS of $0.48 beat estimates by $0.04, but revenue of $11.21B missed by $140M; shares fell 6.24% after-hours to $32.96.
*   Gross margin improved 60bps to 42.8% on supply-chain gains; North America grew 2% while Greater China plunged 26% amid business reset.
*   Company forecasts FY2027 revenue decline in high-single digits with EBIT falling more; adjusted EPS guidance of $1.15-$1.35 excludes restructuring.

output.question: What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?

key_facts.fact: Nike reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (quarter ended August 31, 2026) on October 1, 2026: revenues of $11.2 billion, down 4% reported and 5% currency-neutral; gross margin up 60 bps to 42.8%; diluted EPS $0.48; net income $0.7 billion, down 2%.

On the call, CFO Dave Denton announced a new guidance framework: Nike will give a full-fiscal-year outlook and update it through the year, rather than quarter-by-quarter guidance — so no standalone Q2 FY2027 revenue or EPS forecast was issued.

Fiscal 2027 guidance: revenues to decline in the high-single-digit range; EBIT to decline by a greater percentage than revenue (gross margin pressure, fixed-cost deleverage, higher input costs); SG&A to remain down year-over-year.

Quarter-specific color for the current quarter (Q2 FY2027): lapping EMEA Cyber Week promotional activity and a higher North America sell-in comparison represents a revenue headwind of approximately 400 basis points in the second quarter.

Fiscal 2027 adjusted diluted EPS guided to $1.15–$1.35 (excluding ~$0.15 of Pace restructuring expenses), with an effective tax rate in the mid-20 percent range; guidance was well below pre-report consensus of $1.61 EPS and ~$45.31 billion revenue (~-2%).

Nike announced the Pace operating-model transformation: approximately $2.5 billion in cumulative savings through fiscal 2031, ~$1.0 billion of pre-tax charges plus ~$0.3 billion of severance recognized in fiscal 2026 (~$0.3 billion to be recognized in fiscal 2027); restructuring will lead to layoffs beginning in 2027.

Stock reaction: NKE closed at $35.10 on October 1 before the 4:15 p.m. ET release, then fell to $32.78 (-6.6%) in after-hours trading by 4:20 p.m. before recovering to $33.85 (-3.6%) just before the 5 p.m. call; Investing.com cited a 6.24% after-hours fall to $32.96.
The negative reaction extended into the next session: Nike shares dropped again on Friday, October 2, falling for a second straight day after the revenue decline and 2027 layoff plans.

Q1 detail behind the guidance: Greater China revenue fell 26%, EMEA fell 5%, North America grew 2%; NIKE Sportswear fell low-double digits, Jordan Brand fell mid-teens (Dunk revenue cut by nearly half, a ~$200 million Sportswear headwind), while the Nike Performance business grew high-single digits; management plans to share more at an Investor Day in November 2026.
